title: Worked Examples: Adding & Subtracting Directed Numbers
objectives: Solve multi-step addition and subtraction problems involving integers with step-by-step reasoning
Recognize and eliminate common misconceptions like double negative confusion

blocks.heading: Systematic Problem-Solving Method
blocks.content:
When evaluating complex integer expressions like $(-15) - (-8) + (-12) - 4$, follow this standard 3-step strategy:
1. Eliminate consecutive signs: $-(-x) \to +x$ and $+(-x) \to -x$.
2. Group positive terms together and negative terms together.
3. Compute the final difference and attach the appropriate sign.

steps: Step 1: Simplify consecutive signs: -(-9) becomes +9. Expression is (-12) + 7 + 9.
Step 3: Combine (-312) + 231. Magnitudes: 312 and 231. 312 > 231, so sign is negative.

takeaways: Always convert subtraction into addition of the additive inverse: a - b = a + (-b).
Minus followed by minus becomes plus: a - (-b) = a + b.
Grouping positives and negatives makes mental arithmetic rapid and error-free.
